interpretation.note: Compare d2_rate_occluded vs d2_rate_clean (does occlusion predict WRONG LABEL specifically) against any_failure_rate_occluded vs any_failure_rate_clean (does it predict general difficulty instead). 030's own finding on the production corpus was that stamp/occlusion alone was NOT sufficient explanation (PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, route/OCR/layout interaction mattered more) -- this phase checks whether the same qualitative pattern holds on an independent benchmark, without assuming it must.

caveat: This benchmark has NO true stamp/occlusion category (Phase 1) -- these are the closest available proxies, at PAGE granularity (ambiguous across multi-table pages, per the GT contract's own limitation). A null result here does not prove occlusion is irrelevant to Mechanism D in general, only that these specific proxies on this benchmark don't show it.
